conventions: Every new .ts, .tsx and .js file starts with the Apache 2.0 header block with the year 2026 ('Copyright 2026 The Backstage Authors', same wording as existing headers); never change the year in an existing file.
Formatting is Prettier with the @backstage/cli config: single quotes, trailing commas, 2-space indent, no parentheses around a single arrow parameter (table => {}), 80-column wrapping.
Match the style of the file and package you are in (import order, naming, error handling); consistency within a package beats consistency across the repo.
Imports: keep the existing import blocks of an edited file; add a new name to an existing import from the same module instead of adding a second import of that module; no unused imports.

Never hand-edit anything under **/schema/openapi/generated/**, report*.api.md or report.sql.md; generated code comes from the OpenAPI generator tooling step and reports are regenerated later with yarn build:api-reports.

Every new exported symbol of a published package has TSDoc with a release tag (@public for catalog-model and catalog-client additions); internal files (not exported from a package entry point) need no release tag.

User-facing frontend strings go through the plugin's translation ref (catalogTranslationRef in plugins/catalog/src/alpha/translation.ts, techdocsTranslationRef in plugins/techdocs/src/translation.ts) with useTranslationRef from @backstage/core-plugin-api/alpha.
Tests run on Jest via backstage-cli (CI=true yarn test <path>); describe/it blocks, expect assertions; prefer fewer thorough tests with several assertions each.

Frontend tests use React Testing Library through renderInTestApp (@backstage/test-utils for the old frontend system, @backstage/frontend-test-utils for the new one), query with screen and findBy*, never add test IDs to implementation code.

Backend database tests use TestDatabases.create() from @backstage/backend-test-utils, iterate with describe.each/it.each(databases.eachSupportedId()), and call applyDatabaseMigrations(knex) on a fresh databases.init(databaseId).
Database code is portable knex only (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite); entity refs are stored and compared in lowercase stringified form (kind:namespace/name) exactly as stringifyEntityRef produces them.
Knex migrations are CommonJS files with '// @ts-check', JSDoc '@param {import('knex').Knex} knex' annotations, and both exports.up and exports.down.
Errors come from @backstage/errors; loggers are the LoggerService already held by the class.
Documentation follows docs/contribute/doc-style-guide.md: short sentences, second person, code font for annotation names, paths and endpoints.
Changesets are written by hand as .changeset/<name>.md with YAML front matter naming the package and bump, then one adopter-facing paragraph with no internal function, class or variable names.

decisions.choice: Constant ANNOTATION_FORMER_REFS = 'backstage.io/former-refs' and helper getEntityFormerRefs(entity): string[] both live in the new file packages/catalog-model/src/entity/formerRefs.ts and are re-exported from src/entity/index.ts; the helper returns lowercase stringified refs (stringifyEntityRef form) in first-seen order.
rejected: returning CompoundEntityRef[]
putting the constant in constants.ts and the helper in ref.ts
decisions.reason: Strings are what the backend stores and compares, and one new file keeps the feature together like location/annotation.ts does.

decisions.choice: New table former_entity_refs with columns entity_id (string 255, not null, FK to final_entities.entity_id ON DELETE CASCADE) and former_entity_ref (string 255, not null); unique index former_entity_refs_entity_id_former_entity_ref_uniq on (entity_id, former_entity_ref) and index former_entity_refs_former_entity_ref_idx on (former_entity_ref); migration file 20261109000000_former_entity_refs.js.
rejected: FK to refresh_state.entity_id
storing former refs in the search table
decisions.reason: Rows are written in the same publication transaction as final_entities, the search table already references final_entities, and a dedicated indexed table keeps by-name and search queries untouched (NFR-1).

decisions.choice: performStitching computes getEntityFormerRefs(entity) filtered to refs of at most 255 characters before the publication transaction, then inside the transaction right after syncSearchRows deletes all former_entity_refs rows of entityId and batch-inserts the new rows with BATCH_SIZE; unchanged entities (hash match) skip it like the search rows.
rejected: a minimal diff sync like syncSearchRows
writing outside the publication transaction
decisions.reason: Former refs are a handful of rows per entity, one delete plus one batched insert is what NFR-1 asks for, and a 255-character cap keeps a hostile annotation from failing the stitch on varchar(255).

decisions.topic: Where the lookup lives in the backend
decisions.choice: Add entityByFormerRef(request: EntityByFormerRefRequest): Promise<EntitiesBatchResponse> to the internal EntitiesCatalog interface; DefaultEntitiesCatalog resolves the claim and delegates to its own entitiesBatch; AuthorizedEntitiesCatalog mirrors its entitiesBatch permission logic (DENY gives [null], CONDITIONAL passes the permission filter, ALLOW passes through).
rejected: a separate resolver passed to createRouter through RouterOptions
resolving in the router with own-service credentials
decisions.reason: Reuses the existing read permission and conditional-decision path unchanged, and keeps the router as thin as the by-name route.

decisions.choice: Live name wins: if final_entities has a row whose entity_ref equals the requested ref, the result is [null] regardless of the caller's permissions. Ambiguity: the claim query selects with limit 2; two rows give [null] and a logger.debug line naming the former ref; one row resolves to that row's final_entities.entity_ref.
rejected: checking the live name with the caller's permissions
picking the most recently updated claimant
logging ambiguity at warn on every request
decisions.reason: A live entity hidden from the caller must still block a hijack, picking a winner lets one entity take over another's old name, and a per-request warn would flood logs.

decisions.choice: GET /entities/by-former-name/{kind}/{namespace}/{name}, operationId GetEntityByFormerName (generated client method getEntityByFormerName), 200 returns the Entity schema like by-name, any miss or deny is a 404 NotFoundError with message "No entity found that was formerly named '<name>', with kind '<kind>' in namespace '<namespace>'"; auditor eventId 'entity-fetch' with meta { queryType: 'by-former-name', entityRef: <requested ref> }.
rejected: adding a query flag to the by-name endpoint
a 301 redirect response
decisions.reason: Out of scope 3 forbids touching by-name, and returning the entity body lets the client read its current ref.

a shared helper in plugin-catalog-react
decisions.reason: Router state keeps shared URLs clean and stops a copied link from showing the notice; each plugin only reads its own marker, so no cross-package API is needed.

decisions.choice: A former-ref lookup runs only when the by-ref lookup returned undefined, the location state carries no renamedFromEntityRef marker, and catalogApi.getEntityByFormerRef exists; the lookup itself resolves one hop on the backend.

units.behaviour: Defines the backstage.io/former-refs well-known annotation and a helper that turns an entity's annotation value into normalized former entity refs.
rules: 1. Import Entity from './Entity', DEFAULT_NAMESPACE from './constants', and parseEntityRef, stringifyEntityRef from './ref'.

2. Export const ANNOTATION_FORMER_REFS = 'backstage.io/former-refs' with TSDoc: the value is a comma-separated list of entity refs the entity was previously known by; short refs (name) and namespace/name refs default to the entity's own kind and namespace; tag @public.
3. Export function getEntityFormerRefs(entity: Entity): string[] with TSDoc describing the normalization rules below and @public, @param and @returns tags.
4. Read entity.metadata.annotations?.[ANNOTATION_FORMER_REFS]; when it is not a string, return [].
5. Compute ownNamespace = entity.metadata.namespace || DEFAULT_NAMESPACE and ownRef = stringifyEntityRef({ kind: entity.kind, namespace: ownNamespace, name: entity.metadata.name }).
6. Split the value on ',', trim each item, and skip empty items.
7. Parse each item with parseEntityRef(item, { defaultKind: entity.kind, defaultNamespace: ownNamespace }) inside try/catch; skip the item when parsing throws.
8. Skip the item when parsed.kind.toLowerCase() differs from entity.kind.toLowerCase().
9. Stringify the parsed ref with stringifyEntityRef; skip it when it equals ownRef or was already collected; otherwise append it, so the result keeps first-seen order without duplicates.
10. The function never throws and never mutates the entity.

units.behaviour: Knex migration that creates the former_entity_refs table mapping a normalized former entity ref to the entity that claims it.
rules: 1. CommonJS file: Apache header with 2026, blank line, '// @ts-check', then exports.up and exports.down as named async functions with '/** @param {import('knex').Knex} knex */' JSDoc.
2. up: knex.schema.createTable('former_entity_refs', table => { ... }) with table.comment('Former entity refs that entities declare through the backstage.io/former-refs annotation').
3. Column entity_id: table.string('entity_id').notNullable().references('entity_id').inTable('final_entities').onDelete('CASCADE').comment('The entity that claims the former ref').
4. Column former_entity_ref: table.string('former_entity_ref').notNullable().comment('A former entity ref on lowercase kind:namespace/name form').

5. table.unique(['entity_id', 'former_entity_ref'], { indexName: 'former_entity_refs_entity_id_former_entity_ref_uniq' }) and table.index('former_entity_ref', 'former_entity_refs_former_entity_ref_idx').
6. down: await knex.schema.dropTable('former_entity_refs').
7. No raw SQL and no transaction config override; the default migration transaction is used.

rules: 1. Live name wins: query this.database<DbFinalEntitiesRow>('final_entities').where('final_entities.entity_ref', request.formerRef).select({ entityId: 'final_entities.entity_id' }).first(); when a row exists return { items: { type: 'object', entities: [null] } } without looking at claims. This check never uses the caller's credentials.

2. Claims: query this.database<DbFormerEntityRefsRow>('former_entity_refs').innerJoin<DbFinalEntitiesRow>('final_entities', 'former_entity_refs.entity_id', 'final_entities.entity_id').where('former_entity_refs.former_entity_ref', request.formerRef).select({ entityRef: 'final_entities.entity_ref' }).limit(2).
3. No claim: return { items: { type: 'object', entities: [null] } }.
4. Two claims: call this.logger.debug(`Refusing to resolve former entity ref ${request.formerRef}, it is claimed by more than one entity`) and return { items: { type: 'object', entities: [null] } }.
5. One claim: return this.entitiesBatch({ entityRefs: [claims[0].entityRef], filter: request.filter, credentials: request.credentials }).
6. Do not change entitiesBatch or any other existing method (NFR-1).

Imports: errorApiRef, useApi, useRouteRef, useRouteRefParams from '@backstage/core-plugin-api'; catalogApiRef, EntityLoadingStatus, entityRouteParams, entityRouteRef from '@backstage/plugin-catalog-react'; Entity, stringifyEntityRef from '@backstage/catalog-model'; useEffect from 'react'; useLocation, useNavigate, useParams from 'react-router-dom'; useAsyncRetry from 'react-use/esm/useAsyncRetry'; getRenamedFromEntityRef from './EntityRenamedNotification'.

2. Read { kind, namespace, name } from useRouteRefParams(entityRouteRef), const { '*': subPath = '' } = useParams(), location = useLocation(), entityRoute = useRouteRef(entityRouteRef), navigate, errorApi, catalogApi; renamedFromEntityRef = getRenamedFromEntityRef(location.state).

3. useAsyncRetry(async (): Promise<{ entity?: Entity; renamedTo?: Entity }> => ...) with deps [catalogApi, kind, namespace, name, renamedFromEntityRef]: fetch entity = await catalogApi.getEntityByRef({ kind, namespace, name }); return { entity } when the entity exists, when renamedFromEntityRef is set (loop guard, NFR-6) or when catalogApi.getEntityByFormerRef is undefined.

A useEffect on [value, entityRoute, navigate, subPath, location.search, location.hash, kind, namespace, name] navigates when value?.renamedTo is set: navigate(`${entityRoute(entityRouteParams(value.renamedTo, { encodeParams: true }))}${subPath ? `/${subPath}` : ''}${location.search}${location.hash}`, { replace: true, state: { renamedFromEntityRef: stringifyEntityRef({ kind, namespace, name }) } }).
6. Keep the existing useEffect that posts 'No name provided!' and navigates to '/' when name is missing.

rules: 1. Explain the value is a comma-separated list of entity refs the entity was previously known by; whitespace around items is ignored and empty items are skipped.

2. Explain defaulting: a bare name uses the entity's own kind and namespace, a namespace/name ref uses the entity's own kind; refs with a different kind than the entity, refs that fail to parse and the entity's own ref are ignored; matching is case-insensitive.
3. Show a yaml '# Example:' block with metadata.name new-name and annotation backstage.io/former-refs: old-name, legacy/older-name.

4. Conflict rules: when an entity currently exists with the requested ref, the old ref does not resolve (the live entity wins); when more than one entity declares the same former ref, it resolves to nothing.

5. Permissions: a former ref only resolves to an entity the caller may read; otherwise it behaves as an unknown ref, so the new name is not revealed. Link to the lookup endpoint in api.md (#get-entitiesby-former-namekindnamespacename).

6. Frontend: the catalog entity page and the TechDocs reader redirect an old link to the renamed entity, keep the rest of the path, query string and hash, and show a dismissible notice; only one hop is followed, so list every former ref on the current entity; the index updates the next time the catalog processes the entity after its annotation changes.

units.behaviour: Changeset for @backstage/catalog-model.
rules: 1. Front matter: '@backstage/catalog-model': minor

2. Body: Added the `backstage.io/former-refs` well-known annotation, which lets an entity list the entity refs it was previously known by, along with the `ANNOTATION_FORMER_REFS` constant and a `getEntityFormerRefs` helper that returns those refs in normalized form.

units.behaviour: Changeset for @backstage/catalog-client.
rules: 1. Front matter: '@backstage/catalog-client': minor

2. Body: Added an optional `getEntityByFormerRef` method to `CatalogApi`, implemented by `CatalogClient`, which returns the entity that currently declares a given ref in its `backstage.io/former-refs` annotation, or `undefined` when there is no match. Custom `CatalogApi` implementations do not need to change.

style_from.reason: Changeset format.

units.behaviour: Changeset for @backstage/plugin-catalog-backend.
rules: 1. Front matter: '@backstage/plugin-catalog-backend': minor

2. Body: The catalog now indexes the entity refs that entities list in the `backstage.io/former-refs` annotation and serves them through a new `GET /entities/by-former-name/:kind/:namespace/:name` endpoint, which returns the entity that currently declares the given former ref. A ref that an existing entity holds, or that more than one entity declares, does not resolve, and callers only receive entities they are allowed to read. This release includes a database migration that adds a table for the index.
3. Do not edit report.sql.md or any report*.api.md file; they are regenerated before the pull request (NFR-7).
